methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: The TISM-P method has been used to find the hierarchical relationship among the sustainability factors in the hotel

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Mentions 'energy baseline' and 'energy performance indicator' only aspirationally (framed as an extension of the triple bottom-line sustainability framework). The actual methods (TISM-P, SAP-LAP linkages, flowing stream strategy, rough set theory) model hierarchical/polarity relationships among qualitative sustainability factors and derive IF-THEN rules for hotel service ratings; energy is one factor (SENF3). No energy quantity is measured or normalised and no EnPI/EnB model, functional form, normalisation variables, or estimation approach is characterised. Incidental EnPI/EnB mention within a framework -> methodologically ineligible per the v2.3 registered threshold.

paper_type.evidence_quote: This study presents an in-depth case study of the intersection of sustainability and business strategy in the hotel

stage1.notes: Borderline eligibility. Abstract claims to 'establish a correct baseline and energy performance indicator' (p1); p17 names hotel-level variables (location, service quality, size) for a 'proposed' EnPI, but no energy quantity is measured/normalised and no EnPI/EnB model is operationalised; energy is one qualitative TISM-P factor (SENF3). Sector=hotels (services), also out-of-scope for 3B. Flagged for human check.
